page: Microsoft Azure E32s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU supports x86_64 vector and matrix instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI, along with cryptographic AES instructions. Hardware cache structures include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache.

Memory capacity is configured at 256.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. In synthetic memory bandwidth testing, the architecture yields 1663.4 GB/sec on cached small blocks, with uncached large-block throughput reaching 90.27 GB/sec for reads and 43.64 GB/sec for writes. The instance does not include local disk storage, requiring external Azure premium storage volumes for persistent data. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations position the compute and memory subsystem within the average middle tier. The instance registers a PassMark CPU score of 27507.6 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10843.0, reflecting steady multi-threaded execution for compilation and general system tasks. In in-memory data store tests, the server processes 26.54 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-bound machine learning tasks demonstrate limited capability on large language models, achieving 47.23 tokens per second on prompt ingestion for 7B models and falling to 4.56 tokens per second on 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E32s_v4 delivers strong memory density per compute core, making it economically rational for workloads constrained by memory capacity rather than raw compute speed or GPU acceleration. Primary workload targets include large-scale in-memory databases like Redis, enterprise relational database management systems, big data analytics engines, and medium-scale enterprise software applications.

It offers 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, supported by 256.0 GB of system memory, which establishes an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The architecture incorporates AVX-512 instructions, a 35 MB L3 cache, and zero bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on remote managed disks. Benchmark measurements fall consistently within the median range, delivering a Geekbench multi-core score of 10843.0, a PassMark CPU rating of 27507.6, and 26.54 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth tests yield 90.27 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 43.64 GB/sec for writes. Because of its large memory allocation relative to compute cores, the E32s_v4 functions efficiently for enterprise relational databases, large-scale in-memory caching systems, and heavy memory-bound data processing pipelines.
